entry.dc:title: RESEARCH AND APPLIED TECHNOLOGY SYMPOSIUM ON MINED-LAND RECLAMATION, PAPERS, 1973.
entry.dc:creator: Symp
entry.dc:description: During recent years significant progress has been achieved in developing the technology necessary to restore to productive uses the land disturbed during surface mining. Papers presented at the Symposium cover not only the standard reclamation topics of grading, soil amendments, plant materials, and planting methods, but also preplanning the mining operation and mine operating procedures. In many cases a more productive land use can be attained through reclamation, and papers presented at the final session are devoted to utilization and management of mined-land. Individual papers are provided with bibliographic references.

entry.dc:title: EQUIPMENT NEEDS TO MEET THE CHLLENGE OF SURFACE MINING OF COAL AND URANIUM IN THE DECADE AHEAD.
entry.dc:creator: Ritchie M.
entry.dc:description: This paper focuses on the 1975-1985 period in attempting to demonstrate the equipment requirements in the coal and uranium industries for that period. In the coal industry, it appears that both stripping and mining equipment needs will grow at a rate of 10-12%/year in the future. This equipment will not be radially different from that used today even though some increases in size will probably occur in some equipment lines. The emphasis will be upon improvement in present generation machinery. The same may also be true in the uranium industry. Growth rates on the order of perhaps 50%/year will be experienced as the utility industry continues to install plants using nuclear fuels. It appears that ost of the equipment will besimilar to that used today.

entry.dc:title: Mined-land reclamation studies on bighorn sheep range in Alberta, Canada
entry.dc:creator: Etter H.M.
entry.dc:description: Several ecological factors combine to make the amount and quality of winter range of great importance for the maintenance of Bighorn Sheep (Ovis canadensis) herds in the Province of Alberta, Canada. Increased resource development activities, particularly surface mining, have posed new problems of land-use and reclamation in the sub-alpine forest zone. Solutions to these problems are being sought in reclamation studies at Luscar, Alberta, with emphasis upon winter sheep-range as an important land-use objective. Hydro-seeding trials have facilitated the selection of promising plant species and varieties for revegetation of mined-land. © 1973.

entry.dc:title: SIMILKAMEEN PROJECT.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Similkameen Mining Co formed in 1967 by the Newmont Mining Corp owns in the vicinity of Princeton, B. C. two main orebodies: the Ingerbelle and Copper Mountain whose total reserves amount to about 76-million tons with a grade of 0. 53% Cu and an average ratio of 2. 2 tons of waste to one ton of ore. These orebodies are separated by the deep canyon of the Similkameen river. Paper describes the surface mining operations and equipment used as well as the flotation mill, designed to treat 15,000 tpd of ore. Unusual feature of the project consists of a suspension bridge over the Similkameen Canyon, built to accommodate tailings-, and reclaim water pipelines.

entry.dc:title: DRAMATIC MODERNIZATION PROGRAM IMPROVES OVERALL PRODUCTION AT JEFFREY MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Li T.
entry.dc:description: Title property, owned and operated by Canadian Johns-Manville Ltd. and located 100 m east of Montreal in the city of Asbestos, Que. accounts for approximately 37% of current Canadian production of chrysotile asbestos and about 13% of world production. Believed to be the world's largest asbestos mine, the oval-shaped open pit measures more than a mile at its widest point and is 900 ft deep. Paper describes the steeply dipping ore body and technical innovations involved in the conversion from underground to surface mining that has taken place in the 1960s. New drilling and blasting techniques and haulage of ore and waste in 100 t capacity diesel-electric trucks are outlined. Modernization of ore treatment technique comprises asbestos fiber recovery techniques and fluid bed dryers.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING COAL VIA LONGWALL METHOD.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Paper describes the scope of a study being carried out by the West Virginia Surface Mining & Reclamation Assn. of Charleston, W. Va. that has as its purpose to demonstrate that surface longwall mining of shallow-lying coal seams, 100 ft or less below the surface, will help in controlling acid mine drainage through immediately sealing the exposed coal seam from the air before acid can form. Furthermore, it is expected that the surface over the mined area will settle without shearing, causing minimal environmental disturbance.

entry.dc:title: Effect of Gravitational Forces on Development of the Static Groundwater Table.
entry.dc:creator: Kyziol S.
entry.dc:description: Paper postulates that the formation of a statical groundwater level in the mines depends also of pulling forces, being exerted by the overlying rock strata. This phenomenon should be taken under consideration in plan of surface mining exploitation because the groundwater table may be lowered on account of the removal of overburden.

entry.dc:title: WESTERN ENERGY STRIPS THE 25-FT ROSEBUD IN SOUTHEASTERN MONTANA.
entry.dc:creator: Cornforth C.
entry.dc:description: Western Energy Co. of Butte, Mont, a wholly owned subsidiary of Montana Power Co. , has reserves of 850-million tons of low sulfur (0. 7%S), sub-bituminous coal (8. 0% ash, averaging 8700 Btu), located near Colstrop, 100 mi east of Billings, Mont, the surface mining operation of the 25-ft thick Rosebud seam producing at present over 5-million tpy of coal (with a 1977 target of 12-13 million tpy) are described.

entry.dc:title: WOODSREEF ASBESTOS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Barraba asbestos mine and mill, located in north eastern part of New South Wales and operated by the Chrysotile Corp. of Australia Ltd, wholly owned subsidary of Woodreef Mines Ltd. has total reserves of 90-million tons of ore thus placing the deposit among the six biggest asbestos mines in the free world. Surface mining, and ore treatment methods at the rate of 5,800 tons/mo. are described.

entry.dc:title: SCOOP ON SHOVELS, LOADERS, AND DRAGLINES.
entry.dc:creator: White L.
entry.dc:description: Based on information derived from American manufacturers of bucketed surface mining equipment, the paper presents new developments in the design of shovels, draglines, and front-end wheel loaders. Other topics include: ways to obtain better equipment, the relationship of Federal regulations to cost increases, and the competitiveness of the big new front-end loaders with shovels in pit production.

entry.dc:title: Limiting Characteristic Data of Steel-Cable-Reinforced Conveyor Belts.
entry.dc:creator: Lachmann H.
entry.dc:description: In surface mining operations at the lignite district of Cologne, West Germany, steel-cable-reinforced conveyor belting with an ultimate tensile strength of 5400 kp/cm (over 100 tons/cm of width) is being used. Should conveying be introduced on a larger scale in the future to relieve transportation of bulk materials by road, rail, or water, much larger installations would be needed. Paper analyzes the limitations involved in construction of this type of belting, weight of belts, vulcanization techniques, required width of the belt for various tensile strength, as well as in drives, and concludes that the ultimate tensile strength of 10,000 kp/cm (about 200 tons/cm of width) appears to be the limit.

entry.dc:title: BULGARIAN NON-FERROUS METAL MINING IN FULL DEVELOPMENT.
entry.dc:creator: Derlipanski D.
entry.dc:description: Today non-ferrous metal mining and metallurgy is a rapidly expanding industry in Bulgaria holding an important position in the national economy. This fact is proven by statistics which show that between 1947 and 1971 the production of llead-zinc-, and copper ores has increased from 96,000 and 25,000 tons to 4,451,000 and 9,509,000 tons respectively. Paper includes a map showing the Bulgarian non-ferrous metal ore deposits and main mining and metallurgical centers. Lead-zinc ore bodies are mined by underground methods whereas surface mining prevails in copper mining. Metallurgical developments are reported.

entry.dc:title: TAILINGS REMOVAL PROJECT OPENS NEW HORIZONS FOR RESLURRYING PROCESS.
entry.dc:description: Mill tailings from the copper ore treatment plant operated in the Philippines by the Atlas Consolidated Mining and Dev. Co are pumped 16 mi away from shore into the ocean. Since the pipeline is of service approximately 10% of the time the tailings have to be temporarily impounded. Lack of suitable space for a new tailing pond led to adopting the Marconaflo process for reslurrying the tailings in a deep pond. Paper discusses many other potential applications of the process in vat or heap leaching, surface mining etc.

entry.dc:title: Significance of wathering in a pennsylvanian sandstone to pollution from strip mines
entry.dc:creator: Grube W.E.
entry.dc:description: WE discuss here some of the factors relevant to the formation of acid in the spoil heaps that result from surface mining of the Upper Freeport coal in northern West Virginia. The coal is overlaid by the Lower Mahoning sandstone<sup>1</sup>, a uniform, quartzose, channel-fill sandstone that can be 30 to 50 feet thick. Pyrite (FeS<inf>2</inf>) is the chief acid-forming species in the sandstone<sup>2</sup>. © 1972 Nature Publishing Group.

entry.dc:title: CONQUISTA, CONOCO-PIONEER U//3O//8 VENTURE, ON STREAM.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Development of the uranium ore mining and milling complex at Fall City, Tex, producing over 600,000 t/yr of ore and 1. 5 million lb of U//3O//8, from small and scattereed deposits by surface mining, required careful planning and versatile equipment because of the wide range of operating conditions encountered.

entry.dc:title: CONQUISTA MINES WIDE-RANGING SOUTH TEXAS URANIUM DEPOSITS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The Conquista Project - a uranium mining and milling complex owned jointly by Continental Oil Co. and Pioneer Nuclear, Inc - began processing uranium ore near Falls City, Tex. , in February 1972. Mine output from open pits will total 600,000 tpy of ore, from which uranium will be extracted by acid leach, solvent extraction, concentration, and precipitation. Surface mining techniques and milling 2000 tpd of ore are described. Flowsheet of the mill is shown.

entry.dc:title: MINING GUIDEBOOK.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Mining Guidebook discusses recent developments in: initial planning; continuous, longwall, and conventional mining; roof control; haulage and hoisting; ventilation fundamentals; mine drainage and acid mine water treatment; surface mining; coal preparation and unit-train loading; maintenance engineering; efficient power designs; purchasing and warehousing; and safety.

entry.dc:title: MERITS OF OPEN PIT VS. UNDERGROUND MINING IN BUTTE.
entry.dc:creator: Hannifan M.K.
entry.dc:description: Paper describes development of mining in the Butte, Mont. mineral district over the past 25 yrs, characterized by block caving (1947-1962), vein stoping (1880 to present) and surface mining (1955 to present) and analyzes the first and third method from viewpoints of cutoff grade, outstanding reserves, and cost of mining. (Block caving was discontinued in 1962 because of interference with surface mining in the same area. ) Potential novel methods (open pit with high discard ratio offset by leach dump credits or underground low grade-high efficiency) are mentioned.

entry.dc:title: ACID MINE DRAINAGE WORKSHOP.
entry.dc:creator: Ahmad M.
entry.dc:description: Proceedings contains: presented papers; examination of problems and/or technologies encountered during field trips; and discussion. Among topics covered were: rate of pyrite oxidation and acid production in the field; deep mine sealing; hydrological approach to control acid pollution; the legal framework of acid mine drainage control; acid mine drainage abatement in surface mining; and reclamation of land and of toxic spoilbanks.

entry.dc:title: SHORTWALL: A WAY TO BOOST PRODUCTION.
entry.dc:creator: Zachar F.
entry.dc:description: For ecological reasons greater emphasis as before is being placed in this country on the underground coal mining vs surface mining. This poses economical problems since the productivity in underground mining has been going down, thus raising the cost of production. It would appear that a solution may be found in converting, hitherto most popular room-and-pillar mining system, to the shortwall (about 150 ft long face) system that permits a better utilization of mechanical equipment (continuous coal miners, self advancing, hydaulic steel supports, conveyors etc) as well as improving the ventilation and dust control.

entry.dc:title: Land application of solid waste
entry.dc:creator: Jackson G.B.
entry.dc:description: The above beneficial aspects of land application of solid waste can be utilized most effectively in reclaiming stripped surface soils near abandoned surface mining operations. The adaptation of the environment in this manner toward the treatment of a suitable solid waste represents a least cost approach in order to obtain maximum waste treatment with maximum future land benefits. In this instance, suitable wastes become environmental assets rather than environmental polluters.

entry.dc:title: THE WAY THE MONEY GOES IN OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: While the operating costs in surface mining operations can vary from as little as 17 to over 130 cents/ton, it is possible to determine meaningful figures for industry as a whole. Article presents a summary that outlines the broad cost patterns for the major functions within open pit operations and gives overall estimates for both operating and capital expenditure.

entry.dc:title: WHEN ARE WE GOING TO MINE OIL?
entry.dc:creator: Herkenhoff E.
entry.dc:description: Precarious state of energy supply in this country calls for examination of hitherto unexploited sources of fuels. Paper points out that there exist 383 shallow(less than 900 ft deep) oil fields plus deposits of oil sand and oil shales all of which could and should be exploited by surface mining combined, wherever necessary, with hot water processing. Preliminary economics for a domestic operation are analyzed.

entry.dc:title: CURRENT DRILLING AND BLASTING PRACTICES IN OPEN PIT MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Bauer A.
entry.dc:description: Among the recent trends in drilling and blasting practice in surface mining, as reviewed in the paper, the growing popularity of large rotary drills, replacing the percussive drills, has been noted. Hole sizes range up to 15-in. 30-in. diam holes have been tried in materials that freeze or set like concrete during winter (tar sands in Canada). ANFO and slurries predominate in open pits; slurries, however, have continued to expand in usage and applications. Effect of good blasting fragmentation on performance of power shovels is stressed.

entry.dc:title: Are Landowners Underpaid or Overpaid for Surface Mining Mineral Rights? Real Investment Values and Original Market Prices of Land in Eastern Kentucky
entry.dc:creator: Howard H.
entry.prism:publicationName: American Journal of Economics and Sociology
